name: math_differentiating

phase_0.boundary_condition: the field of real analysis and the definition of the derivative

VINIT.justification: the state before a specific function or variable is declared

TANCH.justification: the final closed result containing the rate of change for the entire domain

AFWD.justification: the forward movement from a point to its neighbor in the domain

AREV.justification: the reverse operation to find the difference between the mapped values

CLINK.justification: the composition of the difference and the division by the increment

IMSCRIB.justification: the identity where the secant line becomes the tangent line at a single point

FSPLIT.justification: the branching of the quotient into a determinate value or an undefined singularity

FFUSE.justification: the reunification of the left and right limits into a single derivative value

EVALT.justification: the affirmative state where the limit exists and is finite

EVALF.justification: the negative state where a cusp or discontinuity prevents differentiation

ENGAGR.justification: the simultaneous presence of vanishing numerator and denominator before resolution

IFIX.justification: the permanent fixation of a power or chain rule into the mathematical record

phase_2.split_input: the difference quotient at a point
phase_2.fuse_result: the difference quotient at a point

phase_3.void_description: an empty coordinate system without defined mappings
phase_3.true_description: a smooth continuous curve with a defined slope
phase_3.false_description: a jump discontinuity or vertical asymptote
phase_3.both_description: a removable singularity where the limit exists but the point is displaced

steps.domain_action: initialize the function f(x) in the real domain
identify the specific point x for local analysis
apply an infinitesimal increment h to the input
calculate the change in output f(x+h) minus f(x)
compose the ratio of output change to input change
evaluate the limit as h approaches zero from both directions
confirm the existence of a finite limit on the primary branch
detect any potential discontinuity on the secondary branch
hold the indeterminate 0/0 state during algebraic simplification
converge the directional limits into a single derivative value
record the resulting derivative function into the table of integrals
seal the operation as the completed gradient of the function
